name: AI governance, risk and audit
oneLiner: Regulation creates a function; the function creates the jobs.
why: Independently checking the work is the whole point — the builder cannot audit the builder
Conformity obligations need named owners and documented evidence
Insurers and boards are asking for both
threats: The headline ratios come from a vendor study with a commercial interest in governance hiring
Enforcement timelines keep moving, which delays hiring plans

metrics.label: Consultant day rate in mature markets

claims.text: Across eight EU countries, companies are hiring roughly seven professionals to build AI systems for every one hired to govern them.
Independent AI governance consultants in mature markets command day rates of $800–$2,000, with demand up 150% year over year.
Governing work is a permanent function once regulation attaches to it: EU AI Act obligations, NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001 all need evidence that someone checked the system.
